figure_checks.caption_independence: The caption is not a restatement of a title; the figure carries no title at all. It names the device and the measurement conditions ('One reserved H200 for the repaired-head measurement, warm execution after compilation, read included'), states the allocation total (27.352 s) and that every lane converged, and describes the axis and weights. It does work the figure cannot do, and it agrees with what the render shows.
figure_checks.clipping: Attached render 1399x720: the outer 1, 2, 3 and 8 px frames contain zero non-white pixels. Ink spans x=163-1344 and y=35-649, so nothing is cut at any edge.
figure_checks.contrast_measurement: Measured from the render: label and tick glyphs (82,81,78), axis label (11,11,11), blue series core (40,110,174), grey series core (146,146,146), left spine (82,81,78), bottom spine (125,125,122). Contrasts computed against pure white (255,255,255) at all four corners.
figure_checks.pixel_measurement: Axis mapping from the five x tick label centres: 0.0 at x=349, 0.5 at x=583.5, 1.0 at x=818.5, 1.5 at x=1052.5, 2.0 at x=1287, i.e. 234.5 px per half second and 469 px per second, linear as the brief requires. Marker centres taken as the centre of each thick column run: prototype (grey #929292, row y=121-135) at x=1006 giving 1.400 s against the table's 1.398 s; staged one slice (blue #286eae, row y=306-319) at x=652 giving 0.646 s against 0.645 s; staged sixteen slices (blue, row y=490-504) at x=1150.5 giving 1.709 s against 1.710 s. All three land within one pixel of the recorded walls, in the recorded order.
figure_checks.render_provenance: Only image-0.png (1399x720 RGBA) was opened. It matches plot.py:64's figsize=(14, 7.2) at dpi=100 (1399 px is matplotlib's integer rounding of 1400) and plot.py:50's CANVAS=1400x720. Decoding the marks against the axis and reconciling them with the evidence table is what establishes this PNG as the figure under review rather than a lookalike: see pixel_measurement.

rubric.contrast: pass. Sampled from the render, not from source: all row and tick labels are (82,81,78) = #52514e at 7.94:1 on white, the axis label is (11,11,11) = #0b0b0b at 19.68:1, the blue subject series is (40,110,174) = #286eae at 5.34:1 and the grey comparison (146,146,146) = #929292 at 3.11:1. Every glyph clears the 4.5:1 text threshold by at least 76 per cent, and the only mark below that threshold is a data stroke, which the style floors at 3:1.
rubric.data_ink: pass. The marks are three value stems from the axis to a filled end disc, three x tick marks, two spines and the text; measured non-white coverage is 1.84 per cent of the canvas and every mark either encodes a measurement or carries a scale. Nothing is drawn in a second channel for its own sake: the series are separated by hue and stroke weight alone and both magnitudes are already carried by the stem length.
rubric.decoration: pass. All four canvas corners are pure white and there is no fill, gradient, drop shadow, reference band or box anywhere on the panel. Top and right spines are absent by plot.py:84 and the grid is off at plot.py:85, so no furniture competes with the three stems.
rubric.label_collision: pass. The outer 8 px frame of the 1399x720 render is entirely white, so nothing is clipped. The row label bands are disjoint and their right edges coincide at x=335, six pixels clear of the tick marks at x=341-348; the x tick labels sit in disjoint groups (0.0 at 335-363, 0.5 at 570-597, 1.0 at 805-832, 1.5 at 1039-1066, 2.0 at 1273-1301) and the axis label occupies y=629-648 below them. No label overlaps another label, a marker or a stem.
rubric.legibility: pass. Three horizontal lollipop rows on one linear seconds axis, labelled top to bottom 'prototype · 1 slice', 'staged · 1 slice', 'staged · 16 slices', under the axis label 'Converged solve wall per slice [s]'. The axis now ticks at round values 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0, so the earlier arbitrary scale is gone and the reader can place each mark within a half-second band. The comparison reads at a glance: the grey prototype stem runs to 1.40 s against the staged single-slice stem at 0.65 s, and the staged sixteen-slice stem is the longest at 1.71 s. Glyphs render crisp at the delivered 1399 px width with row labels 19 px tall and the axis label 21 px. The one deduction is the absent value labels, finding 1.
rubric.table_form: pass. This is a comparison of three magnitudes on one shared linear axis, and what it exists to convey is their ordering and relative gap — the staged single-slice solve reaching about 46 per cent of the prototype's wall, and the sixteen-slice row about 2.6 times the single-slice staged row. The same page states the exact walls, steps, refactors, reads and frozen/unfrozen counts in a table directly above the figure, so the image is not standing in for tabular data.

findings.disposition_note: The three values are stated exactly in the evidence table above the figure and the ordering is unambiguous, so no reader is misled; value labels are a refinement for a later figure pass rather than a reason to hold this node.
findings.summary: No value is printed at any marker, and every measurement falls between the round ticks: 0.645 s between 0.5 and 1.0, 1.398 s between 1.0 and 1.5, 1.710 s between 1.5 and 2.0. The number this node exists to report is the staged single-slice wall of 0.645 s, and a reader can only get it by interpolating against a half-second grid; the 2.17x speed-up over the prototype is likewise read as an approximate ratio rather than a stated one. The ordering and the rough gaps are still unambiguous at a glance, and the exact walls are carried in the table immediately above the figure on the same page, which is why this does not hold the node. A single right-of-marker value label per row would fix it.

findings.disposition_note: Grey is the style's reference colour and the row is separately labelled and marked, so the lightening costs nothing that is needed to read the figure; choosing a darker reference tone belongs to a later redraw.
findings.summary: The prototype comparison row is stroked #929292, which measures 3.11:1 against white, while the axes it is read against are darker: the left spine is #52514e at 7.94:1 and the bottom spine #7d7d7a at 4.13:1. The reference series is therefore the faintest ink in the panel, lighter than the furniture around it, so at a glance the baseline stem can read as an axis element rather than as a measured series. It is never actually lost, because it is stroked at 2.6 pt against the subject's 3.0 pt and terminated by a 14 px disc, and the row is named on the y axis.

findings.disposition_note: The metric is the one the reviewed run's brief defined ('the per-slice converged-solve wall ... at one slice and at 16 lanes') and the caption carries the total the division is made from, so the figure is not misleading to a reader who reads the caption; a metric note belongs to a later figure pass.
findings.summary: The sixteen-slice row plots batch['per_slice_ms'] — 27352.07 ms of allocation wall divided by sixteen lanes, 1709.5 ms — as a single marker drawn identically to the two single-solve walls beside it. It is an amortised throughput figure, not the wall any one solve took (every lane ran concurrently and the batch ran until its slowest lane converged, with per-lane steps spanning 4 to 33), and its spread across lanes is not shown, so a reader can take 1.710 s for the duration of one sixteen-lane solve. The caption discloses the 27.352 s total and that every lane converged, from which the division can be reconstructed, which is why this does not hold the node; saying on the axis or beside the row that the sixteen-lane value is per-slice throughput would remove the ambiguity.

item_verdicts.caption: Read and judged only for whether it repeats the figure's title: it does not, and it independently states the device, the conditions, the batch total and the axis construction. No caption defect recorded.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Three non-blocking findings and no blocking finding. Nothing is clipped (zero non-white pixels in the outer 8 px frame), no label overlaps a label, a marker or a stem (row labels end 6 px short of their tick marks), all text measures at least 7.94:1 on white, and all three series are visible with their markers intact, so none of the blocking categories is met and the figure does not hold the node.

item_verdicts.scope: Read-only. No file was edited, created, moved, deleted, redrawn, relabelled or reformatted; the only writes are this record at its two declared paths and the run manifest.
